SEM-001.recommendation: Remove the `requestBody` from GET, HEAD and DELETE operations (move inputs to query/path parameters or reconsider the method)
SEM-001.rationale: RFC 9110: request bodies on GET/HEAD/DELETE have no defined semantics; many proxies, caches, and client SDKs drop or reject them

SEM-002.rationale: RFC 9110: 204 No Content must not carry a body; clients and gateways that enforce this will fail

SEM-003.recommendation: Define at least one scheme in `components.securitySchemes` and apply it via top-level `security`
SEM-003.rationale: An API with no declared security scheme is documented as fully anonymous — a known security trap; even public APIs should state auth explicitly

SEM-004.recommendation: Move credential or secret query parameters (e.g. `api_key`, `password`, `token`) to a request header or request body
SEM-004.rationale: Credentials and secrets in query strings leak into server logs, browser history, and referrer headers (OWASP API Security)

SEM-005.recommendation: Add at least one 4xx (or `default`) error response to every operation that documents only successes
SEM-005.rationale: Consumers cannot handle failures that are not documented; every operation can at minimum fail validation or authorization

SEM-006.recommendation: Change `201` responses on GET and HEAD operations to `200`
SEM-006.rationale: 201 Created signals resource creation; returning it from a read operation misleads clients and tooling

SEM-007.recommendation: Consider renaming verb path segments (e.g. `getUsers`, `delete-order`) to nouns and letting the HTTP method carry the action
SEM-007.rationale: REST models resources as nouns; verbs in paths duplicate the HTTP method and create redundant endpoints over time

SEM-008.recommendation: Consider returning `201` (with a `Location` header) instead of `200` from POST operations that create a resource
SEM-008.rationale: 201 tells clients a resource was created and where to find it; 200 is ambiguous for creation. Skip if this POST is an action/search, not a create

SEM-009.recommendation: Consider adding pagination parameters (e.g. `limit`/`offset` or `cursor`) to GET collection operations
SEM-009.rationale: Unbounded collection responses degrade as data grows; retrofitting pagination later is a breaking change

SEM-010.recommendation: Consider representing monetary properties as a string or integer of minor units instead of `float`/`double`
SEM-010.rationale: Binary floating point cannot represent decimal currency exactly; rounding errors accumulate in monetary arithmetic

SEM-011.recommendation: Consider aligning property naming to a single convention across `components.schemas`
SEM-011.rationale: Mixed naming conventions force consumers to special-case fields and suggest the API grew without a style guide

SEM-012.recommendation: Consider documenting `401` and/or `403` responses on secured operations
SEM-012.rationale: Secured operations can always fail authentication or authorization; documenting it lets clients handle it uniformly

SEM-013.recommendation: Consider defining `properties` or explicitly setting `additionalProperties` on free-form object schemas
SEM-013.rationale: A fully free-form object gives consumers and codegen tools nothing to validate or generate against

SEM-014.recommendation: Consider adding an explicit version (e.g. `/v1`) to the server URL or base path
SEM-014.rationale: Without a versioning scheme, the first breaking change forces an ad-hoc migration strategy on every consumer
